hyperedges.label: Cascade loop: scale -> sample weather -> DC PF -> trip -> attribute -> write
Shared engine-tool contract (copilot fronts siting and line-upgrade tools)
Counterfactual do-operator: seeded twin + site + run_scenario(net=) -> counterfactual_runs
Demo step 5: 'Why this site over the one near Houston?' flow
Shared DuckDB contract tables produced by ingest
Idea 2 data-center pipeline (ingest → resolve → reality → score → cost → tools)
Line-upgrade ranking pipeline (congestion + DLR + reconductor to MW per $M with FERC/SPARK flags)

nodes.label: DuckDB (data/duck/grid.duckdb)
nodes.rationale: One file, no PostGIS this weekend; geometry as WKB or lon/lat. The DuckDB file is the hand-off artifact between units and makes the demo air-gappable (a judge hook).

nodes.label: tests/test_idea1_contract.py (schema snapshot)
nodes.rationale: Guards that adding Idea 2 code leaves the 00-overview tables and tools untouched.

nodes.label: Registry Ingest (pipelines/dc/ingest_*.py)
nodes.rationale: One module per source; developer names normalised via a hand-curated ~40-entry alias table; stages mapped to 7 canonical values.

nodes.label: Idea 2: Data Center Load Verification + Grid Impact Scoring
nodes.norm_label: idea 2: data center load verification + grid impact scoring
nodes.rationale: Ranked #2; strongest standalone if the format allows two entries or judges want something narrower and nearer-term. Reconciles announced/queued/forecast/operating data-center load; phantom load is an anti-fraud framing.

nodes.label: Idea 3: Transmission Line Upgrade Prioritization
nodes.rationale: Ranked #3 because no one on the panel is a transmission engineer; folded into Idea 1 as one screen. Ranks lines by MW unlocked per dollar for DLR vs reconductoring.

nodes.label: Shared Technical Stack
nodes.rationale: DuckDB+Parquet, PostGIS, networkx; PUDL/gridstatus/Globus ingest; pandapower + PyPSA-USA + IEEE 738; LightGBM/PyG/DoWhy/EconML/pgmpy; deck.gl + MapLibre; tool-calling LLM that narrates and never computes.

nodes.label: Line inventory (HIFLD owner + Form 1 conductor join)
nodes.norm_label: line inventory (hifld owner + form 1 conductor join)
nodes.rationale: Synthetic lines joined to real HIFLD geometry by Hausdorff <= 5 km and kV class to attach an owner and a real 'twin of record'; conductor from FERC Form 1 sched 422 else a kV-class ACSR default. Match rate is printed, never hidden.

nodes.label: ERCOT Large Load Interconnection Status report
nodes.norm_label: ercot large load interconnection status report
nodes.rationale: ERCOT first because the report is a single public spreadsheet.

nodes.label: FERC docket RM26-4 + Section 206 show-cause responses
nodes.norm_label: ferc docket rm26-4 + section 206 show-cause responses

nodes.label: 04 Siting Engine Spec
nodes.rationale: Rank Texas sites for the next firm nuclear GW using two independent scores (safety/buildability and grid value) plus a regulatory-path label, so the copilot can answer siting questions from tool results rather than opinion.

nodes.label: 08 Line Upgrade Screen Spec
nodes.rationale: Answer 'which lines first?' for grid-enhancing technologies by estimating congestion $/yr, DLR uplift (IEEE 738), reconductoring uplift and cost, ranking by MW per $M, applying the FERC DLR ANOPR screen and flagging DOE SPARK eligibility.

nodes.label: 09 Backup: Data-Center Load Verification Spec
nodes.rationale: Backup, not on critical path; built only if judges want narrower/nearer-term, format allows two entries, or Idea 1 path is green by Day 2 noon. Deck is built regardless. All tables namespaced dc_* so they coexist with Idea 1 in one DuckDB without touching its tables.

nodes.label: Final Recommendation (Idea 1 headline, 3 embedded, 2 backup)
nodes.rationale: All three run on the same stack, so Day 1 shared data work is not wasted whichever is led with.

nodes.label: Fixture DuckDB (make_fixture_db.py)
nodes.rationale: Unblocking rule: ~20 buses, 30 lines, 5 counties, one synthetic scenario so units 02-08 can start before real ingest finishes. Gate A at Day 1 noon.

nodes.label: Model Narrates, Tools Compute
nodes.rationale: Anti-hallucination design: every number in a copilot answer comes from a visible tool call; every regulatory claim comes from cite() with page reference. The LLM never does arithmetic.

nodes.label: Shared Contract (tables, scenarios, tools)
nodes.rationale: Overview owns no data but defines exact table/column/tool/scenario names so 6+ parallel units can build independently; the overview wins any disagreement with a downstream spec.

nodes.label: Real geometry is overlay only, never joined
nodes.norm_label: real geometry is overlay only, never joined
nodes.rationale: HIFLD/OSM real_lines and real_substations are map overlays; synthetic ACTIVSg topology stays synthetic and the demo says so explicitly to avoid implying real-grid fidelity.

nodes.label: add_unit (pro-rata displacement)
nodes.rationale: Existing gens scaled down pro-rata so total gen equals load (DC PF constraint) — the honest 'displaces marginal gen' assumption; ignores unit commitment.

nodes.label: SiteCard panel
nodes.rationale: All values equal POST /site-score for that id; customer-hours avoided is shown only if returned by the API, never computed in the UI.

nodes.label: Blackstart Reach (graph proxy)
nodes.rationale: Greedy BFS over in-service >=138 kV lines within 3 hops and unit_mw cumulative load; a graph metric, not a transient-stability claim, and the card says so.

nodes.label: OR-SAGE (ORNL/TM-2012/403)
nodes.rationale: Re-implemented on open layers because the ORNL exclusion/avoidance criteria are the accepted siting screen; thresholds marked UNVERIFIED must be read from the PDF before demo.

nodes.label: Regulatory-path label
nodes.rationale: One label per site by first match: doe_authorized_federal_land, advance_act_brownfield, nrc_tier1_low_density, nrc_tier2_societal_risk, dod_installation, excluded. DOE/DoD authorization pathways are legally fuzzy — label with caveats, never assert.

nodes.label: Dynamic Line Rating (DLR) uplift
nodes.rationale: dlr_uplift_mw = P50 over the year of max(0, dlr_rating - static_rating); cost $40k/mile + $60k floor anchored on PPL's ~$32k/mile deployment.

nodes.label: IEEE 738 steady-state ampacity
nodes.rationale: Heat balance q_c + q_r = I^2 R + q_s; calibrated to the case rating so synthetic ratings and physics agree; simplifications (fixed solar, 45 deg wind, no cloud) bias uplift upward, bounded by P50 and a 60 % sanity cap. Anchor: Drake 795 ACSR ~900 A.

nodes.label: Reconductoring uplift (advanced conductors)
nodes.rationale: Multiplier 1.5-2.0x for ACSR to ACCC/ACSS per GridLab 2024, capped at 2.0 by terminal equipment; per-mile costs from LBNL REFA are placeholders until read.

nodes.label: DOE SPARK NOFO eligibility
nodes.rationale: SPARK awards are $10-250M projects with >= 50 % cost share, so single short lines are eligible only inside an owner-level bundle >= $10M; the flag is computed on the bundle and propagated to member lines.

nodes.label: FERC DLR ANOPR RM24-6 screen
nodes.rationale: ferc_screen_pass = heavily congested (>= $500k/yr) AND windy (mean wind >= 3 m/s); thresholds are our operationalization of the ANOPR's concept and live in params.yaml with a note.

nodes.label: Siting break-it probes
nodes.rationale: Replace add_unit with a no-op: lol_reduction test MUST fail, proving grid value is a real intervention; swap PAD-US for empty layer: Big Bend S6 test MUST fail.

nodes.label: Combined score (geometric mean)
nodes.rationale: combined = sqrt(safety) x sqrt(grid_value) so a zero safety score zeros the site; ties broken by lol_reduction_mwh.

nodes.label: Population-density downgrade under proposed 10 CFR 53.530
nodes.rationale: Under NRC's July 2026 proposed rule an S1 failure becomes an avoidance penalty (0.4) and the site is labelled nrc_tier2_societal_risk; Tier 1/Tier 2 is pitch vocabulary, the card uses the rule's own language.

nodes.label: Safety Score (exclusion/avoidance)
nodes.rationale: safety_score = 0 if any exclusion fails, else 100 x product of avoidance penalties; every criterion emits a flag with value/threshold/source so the card can cite numbers. A missing layer raises MissingLayerError rather than silently passing.

nodes.label: Hybrid retrieval (BM25 + optional Voyage dense, RRF)
nodes.norm_label: hybrid retrieval (bm25 + optional voyage dense, rrf)
nodes.rationale: BM25 alone is demo-adequate because legal text is heavy on exact terms; dense Voyage embeddings are a Sunday-morning upgrade only if the BM25 eval misses. Chunks never cross a page boundary so page citations are exact.

nodes.label: Line-upgrade break-it probes
nodes.rationale: Replace ieee738_ampacity_a with a wind-blind constant: windy-vs-calm uplift test MUST fail; set the FERC usd_threshold to 0: the < 20 % pass-rate test MUST fail.

nodes.label: Congestion attribution (constraint to line)
nodes.rationale: ERCOT is approximate by design: parse SCED constraint names, fuzzy-match to HIFLD substations, map to synthetic line_id with confidence tiers (exact/fuzzy/unmapped). Unmapped dollars are never spread across lines — reported as unattributed so the demo says what fraction was mapped.

nodes.label: MW per $M ranking
nodes.rationale: mw_per_musd = best of DLR and reconductor uplift per $M cost; best_tech = argmax; sorted within region.

nodes.label: PJM clean reference (PPL DLR corridor)
nodes.rationale: PJM monitored-facility names are tractable, so it validates the constraint-to-line mapper on one known case; used only for the 'our model would have flagged it' demo line, not the Texas ranking. If not reproducible the demo line is cut, not faked.

nodes.label: Twin-derived congestion proxy
nodes.rationale: Where ERCOT constraints do not map, use hours with loading > 90 % in the spec 03 base replay x $20/MWh, tagged congestion_method='twin_proxy' so it is never confused with real shadow prices.

nodes.label: twin.build.build_base_net
nodes.rationale: Stamps element_id from DuckDB contract IDs by MATPOWER row order and fails loudly if counts (2000/2359/0/544/1125) differ; overwrites converter ratings from lines.rate_a_mw.

nodes.label: pandapower.converter.matpower.from_mpc
nodes.rationale: Verified: there is NO pandapower.converter.from_mpc; must pass f_hz=60 (default 50); all 2359 branches import as lines with net.trafo empty.

nodes.label: ACTIVSg2000 (S1)
nodes.rationale: TAMU xlsx is source of record for buses/lines/gens/loads and coordinates; the pip matpower .m is only the electrical model, so no TAMU form and no Globus needed.

nodes.label: Texas First Scope
nodes.rationale: One weekend: ERCOT is a single balancing authority with public hourly load, the best public synthetic grid (ACTIVSg2000), and the best-documented storm (Uri). National is a static scale slide only.

nodes.label: claude-opus-5 via Anthropic SDK
nodes.rationale: Adaptive thinking with medium effort to keep latency under the demo budget; no temperature/prefill/forced tool_choice (rejected on Opus 5); COPILOT_MODEL switchable to claude-sonnet-5 as a rate-limit fallback.

nodes.label: POST /ask (SSE)
nodes.rationale: POST so the client must use fetch + ReadableStream (not EventSource); heartbeat ': ping' every 10 s keeps proxies open.

nodes.label: System prompt (frozen, cache-controlled)
nodes.rationale: ~600 tokens of plain prose; do not over-prescribe because Opus 5 follows short rules well and over-prescription degrades it.

nodes.label: Tool-use loop (agent/loop.py)
nodes.rationale: Manual loop rather than the beta tool runner because SSE must be emitted per tool call/result and timeouts/size caps enforced locally; MAX_ITER 8, 90 s deadline, parallel tool calls returned in one user message, 8 KB result cap.

nodes.label: Post-answer verification (agent/verify.py)
nodes.rationale: Number trace, citation trace, and regulatory-claim guard run after the final text; non-blocking so the demo never stalls, but the UI shows a verified/unverified badge.

nodes.label: Ask panel + SSE parser
nodes.rationale: fetch + ReadableStream with a hand SSE parser because EventSource cannot POST; AbortController per question; call the API origin directly since the Vite proxy buffers SSE.

nodes.label: Never-compute principle
nodes.rationale: The model narrates and plans; it never computes. Every number must come from a tool result and every regulatory claim from a cite hit; if a tool fails the model says so instead of guessing. This is the contract with the judges.

nodes.label: Prompt caching strategy
nodes.rationale: System is a single frozen block with ephemeral cache_control; tools list is a fixed-order constant; volatile UI context goes in the first user message so the cache hits on the second demo question.

nodes.label: Grid Impact Score (models/dc/impact.py)
nodes.rationale: Seven weighted components (flexibility 0.25, headroom 0.20, byog 0.15, load_factor/congestion/service_type/tariff 0.10 each) summing to 1.0; must be deterministic and monotone in each component. Flexibility weight justified by Duke's ~100 GW headroom at 0.5% curtailment.

nodes.label: score_dc_site tool
nodes.rationale: Named score_dc_site rather than score_site to avoid colliding with the Idea 1 tool signature score_site(site_id, unit_mw, scenario_id).

nodes.label: suggest_fixes ('what would make this a 90')
nodes.rationale: Greedy search over a fixed six-item menu, applied one at a time, ordered by delta, stopping at score ≥ 90. months_faster values are demo assumptions labelled on the card.

nodes.label: pipelines.build.export_parquet
nodes.rationale: Parquet mirrors let web/ and notebooks read without taking a DuckDB lock.

nodes.label: Idempotent per-source ingest
nodes.rationale: Every loader is DELETE-by-source-key then insert, and build.py records (source,file,sha256,rows,loaded_at) in ingest_log so a second run changes no row counts and the copilot can cite provenance.

nodes.label: Lead with hit_rate_top20 and peak_statewide_err
nodes.rationale: Class imbalance and spatial autocorrelation inflate AUC, so the operationally honest numbers are top-20 hit rate and statewide peak error.

nodes.label: 6-hour window labels (y_out, frac_out)
nodes.rationale: Max customers_out over the 15-min samples is robust to reporting gaps; y_out = frac_out >= 5% is 'material outage'; windows with no EAGLE-I sample are NULL not zero because a coverage gap is not a zero outage.

nodes.label: HOLDOUT_WINDOWS scenario-based split
nodes.rationale: Scenario windows +-3 days are never in train or calibration; all TX windows from 2024-07-01 onward are excluded to prevent leakage via autoregressive features into Beryl.

nodes.label: sql tool (read-only DuckDB)
nodes.rationale: Rejects anything but SELECT/WITH; row cap 200. Makes every closing-slide number reproducible by pasting one query.

nodes.label: SQL guard (db.py)
nodes.rationale: Read-only connection plus keyword denylist and single-statement check (belt and braces); wrapped as SELECT * FROM (q) LIMIT 201 to detect truncation.

nodes.label: TOOL_SCHEMAS (strict)
nodes.rationale: All six tools strict: true with additionalProperties false so arguments always validate; signatures are the shared contract and must not change.

nodes.label: copilot causal_query tool
nodes.rationale: Every answer carries method, assumptions, and interval so the LLM cannot round 'estimate' up to 'fact'; fails closed to method='unavailable' when artifacts are missing.

nodes.label: line_upgrade_detail side table
nodes.rationale: Additive side table, not in the shared contract, keeps the contract table narrow.

nodes.label: Idea 1: National Grid Digital Twin + Outage Prediction + Nuclear Siting
nodes.norm_label: idea 1: national grid digital twin + outage prediction + nuclear siting
nodes.rationale: Ranked #1 for a defense/national-security/tech-policy judge panel: it is a real systems product with physics under it, CEII-ready and air-gappable, and answers the live 'which base first' procurement question. Six layers: grid model, load/weather, outage prediction, cascade, siting, copilot.

nodes.label: Palantir Chain Reaction (competitor)
nodes.rationale: Workflow and ontology only; no grid physics, no siting engine — positioned as a partner/acquirer rather than a competitor.

nodes.label: L6 Copilot (FastAPI + Claude tool loop)
nodes.rationale: Also serves the thin read APIs (GET /layers/{name}) to the frontend so the web tier never opens DuckDB.

nodes.label: Grid Digital Twin
nodes.rationale: Connects three questions nobody currently connects: where the grid fails, what it cascades into, and where the next gigawatt of firm generation should go. Headline decision already made; do not relitigate.

nodes.label: Line-Upgrade Screen (Idea 3 embedded)
nodes.rationale: Congestion is a twin-loading proxy, DLR uplift is IEEE 738 on county-mean wind, reconductor costs from LBNL REFA; all labelled estimates.

nodes.label: Honest Answers (verbatim in system prompt)
nodes.rationale: Nine pre-written concessions (fake topology, Palantir, nuclear timelines, model quality, cascade realism, not an NRC review, Texas only, line-upgrade estimates, hallucination) placed verbatim in the copilot system prompt so the model never overclaims.

nodes.label: Synthetic Topology (CEII honesty)
nodes.rationale: Real topology is CEII-restricted; synthetic grids are the research standard. Architecture is a slot: swap buses/lines/gens under a data-use agreement and nothing downstream changes. Stated plainly on slide and in copilot system prompt.

nodes.label: Tool-call to map linkage
nodes.rationale: On tool_call the UI reacts (score_site selects the site, run_cascade plays the cascade, predict_outage selects the county, top_lines enters Upgrades mode) — this is what makes demo step 5 visual.

nodes.label: Causal number-trace citation contract
nodes.rationale: answer_numbers and evidence_rows are the only sources a causal numeral may come from; sentences end with [causal:<method>]; intervals crossing zero must be stated as not distinguishable from zero; PDFs are cited only via cite.

nodes.label: models.outage.predict.driver_of
nodes.rationale: Driver = argmax SHAP contribution grouped into ice/wind/heat/wildfire/flood/other; storm_event_* contributions weighted x0.5 because zone->county expansion smears them.

nodes.label: copilot predict_outage tool
nodes.rationale: Serves cached outage_predictions rows when present (cheap, deterministic, citable); the LLM narrates, never computes.

nodes.label: AppState (zustand store)
nodes.rationale: Store actions are the only way to mutate state; there are no API writes.

nodes.label: Demo presets D1-D6 (demo/steps.ts)
nodes.rationale: Every preset must land without a fetch spinner; prefetch on boot for the boot scenario and sites at unitMw=300.

nodes.label: URL state sync
nodes.rationale: No persistence beyond the URL so a demo step is a link.

nodes.label: L3 Outage Model (LightGBM on EAGLE-I)
nodes.rationale: Predicts where and how many customers, not which pole. Three storms held out; held-out AUC shown on screen so accuracy is a demonstrated, not asserted, claim.

nodes.label: uri_2021 scenario (Winter Storm Uri)
nodes.rationale: The hero replay, held out from training; best-documented Texas storm.

nodes.label: 05 Copilot Service Spec
nodes.rationale: One FastAPI process is the single read API for the web app, fronts the four engine tools as routes, and hosts the tool-calling Claude copilot behind POST /ask.

nodes.label: 06 Frontend Spec
nodes.rationale: The one screen the judges see; depends on spec 05 for every byte of data and never reads DuckDB directly. Must carry all six demo steps without reload at 60 fps on the 2000-bus twin.

nodes.label: Grid Value Score
nodes.rationale: 'The number nobody else produces': drop a unit at the site bus, re-run the stress scenario with the SAME seed so the difference is purely the do-operation; weights 40/30/20/10 over LOL reduction, congestion relief, blackstart reach, critical loads protected, min-max normalized per (scenario, unit_mw).

nodes.label: causal.counterfactual.precompute
nodes.rationale: Top-5 site_scores sites at 300 and 1000 MW are precomputed into counterfactual_runs so the demo never waits on pandapower.

nodes.label: Grid-Strength Value Score
nodes.rationale: Put a 300 MW / 1 GW unit at the site in the twin, re-run stress scenarios, measure loss-of-load drop, congestion relief, black-start reach. 'The number nobody else produces.'

nodes.label: cascade_runs table
nodes.rationale: run_id = f"{scenario_id}-s{seed}-{sha8(forced_out)}" owned by spec 03; baseline is seed 0 with no forced outages; spec 04 persists the #1 site's counterfactual run (proposed id uri_2021-s0-cf-<site_id>-1000) so the UI can toggle baseline vs counterfactual.

nodes.label: L4 Cascade Simulation (physics)
nodes.rationale: DC power flow with iterative overload tripping, weather-driven initial failures. Standard academic cascade model, not RTO-grade EMS; the aggregate lost-load and critical-load exposure is the claim, element order is illustrative.

nodes.label: L5 Siting Engine
nodes.rationale: Two scores per site: OR-SAGE/STAND safety screen on open layers plus grid-strength value measured by re-running the cascade with the unit online. The grid-value number is 'the number nobody else produces'.

nodes.label: flux Hackathon Build Specs README
nodes.rationale: Every spec has the same section order (Purpose · Inputs · Outputs · Algorithm · Interfaces · Acceptance · Demo hook · Risks · Time-box); unconfirmed facts are marked [UNVERIFIED].

nodes.label: Counterfactual Replay (site online)
nodes.rationale: Same storm, recommended site online, DoD installation stays green, X million customer-hours avoided — the closing slide. Requires a persisted counterfactual run in cascade_runs with a UI-selectable run_id.

nodes.label: Critical Path 01→03→04→06
nodes.rationale: Data ingest → cascade sim → siting engine → frontend siting screen. Everything else can slip; those four cannot, because the siting counterfactual is the closing slide.

nodes.label: Seeded determinism (seed, scenario_id, hour)
nodes.rationale: Every stochastic choice goes through one numpy Generator seeded by seed ^ hash(scenario_id, hour); same inputs give byte-identical cascade_runs rows, and seed is embedded in run_id. This is what lets spec 07 reuse draws for a proper counterfactual.

nodes.label: Stress-hours evaluation
nodes.rationale: Full 168-h replay x 25 sites x 3 scenarios x 2 unit sizes is hours with pandapower; evaluate only the 12 highest lost-load hours per scenario, share the base run across sites, cache in site_scores. Target < 20 min with lightsim.

nodes.label: Precomputed-table fallback (make seed-demo)
nodes.rationale: Tools read precomputed DuckDB rows and only call live engines on a cache miss, so the copilot demo survives engine lanes finishing late; only uri_2021 rows are required.

nodes.label: C1 — Outage causal Bayesian network
nodes.rationale: Hand-specified (not discovered) discrete DAG weather_severity->exposure->line_failures->substation_loss->customers_out with investment as confounder; answers 'weather vs under-investment' via do() by edge removal. Investment is a SAIDI-trend proxy and middle nodes come from the synthetic twin.

nodes.label: C3 — Counterfactual replay (Uri with site X online)
nodes.norm_label: c3 — counterfactual replay (uri with site x online)
nodes.rationale: Literal do-operation on the twin: reuse the same seeded failure draws (abduction), add a generator via pp.create_gen (action), re-run run_scenario (prediction). It is a function call into spec 03, not new modelling, hence the most real deliverable and the closing slide.

nodes.label: Cost Model (models/dc/cost.py)
nodes.rationale: stranded_cost = phantom_mw × (capacity $1.5M/MW + transmission $0.5M/MW); delay = phantom_mw / queue throughput (fallback 250 MW/month). Every number carries its source string to the UI.

nodes.label: Entity Resolution (pipelines/dc/resolve.py)
nodes.rationale: Blocking + pairwise scoring, no ML: s = 0.40·name + 0.25·geo + 0.20·mw + 0.15·date, link at ≥0.72, connected components. Only ≥0.85 shown in demo to avoid false-positive embarrassment; entity contributes its median MW once (the latent-variable point simplified).

nodes.label: Reality Model (models/dc/reality.py)
nodes.rationale: p_operate = base(stage, iso) × multipliers for co-located gen, min-demand tariff, shopping (1/n_queues), developer track record; clipped 0.02–0.98. Stage priors are labelled 'assumption' informed by LBNL Queued Up (~20% of queued gen reaches COD); intervals via 2000-draw Beta Monte-Carlo so the UI always shows a range.

nodes.label: Entity Resolution / Duplicate Detection
nodes.rationale: Same developer, same MW, three utilities = 'shopping'. Modelled as a latent variable so the aggregate does not triple-count.

nodes.label: Phantom Ratio (announced vs queued vs forecast vs operating)
nodes.norm_label: phantom ratio (announced vs queued vs forecast vs operating)
nodes.rationale: Utilities plan for 90 GW of data-center load by 2030, analysts expect ~65; every phantom gigawatt built for is billions of ratepayer dollars and delay for real loads.

nodes.label: Causal Layer (pgmpy DAG + DoWhy)
nodes.rationale: Answers 'weather vs under-investment' decomposition; writes causal/artifacts/*.json, no shared table; exposed via sql()/API.

nodes.label: Conversion Causal DAG (causal/dc_conversion.py, stretch)
nodes.rationale: DoWhy backdoor adjustment estimating the effect of min_demand_share ≥ 0.75 on energization; only meaningful with ≥100 terminal ERCOT rows, otherwise the honest line 'sample too small; here is the DAG'. The Virginia policy counterfactual is computable from the reality model alone.

nodes.label: Causal-AI Layer (simulator as SCM)
nodes.rationale: The physics simulator IS a structural causal model: interventions are literal do-operations, counterfactuals are re-runs. Learned causality adds an outage causal graph (weather → exposure → line failures → customers out, with utility investment as confounder) and effect estimation via synthetic control / DiD.

nodes.label: HRRR weather (S7)
nodes.rationale: Fetch only needed GRIB messages via herbie byte-range subsetting (2-3 MB/hour instead of 145 MB); ISD station interpolation is the P2 fallback.

nodes.label: P0/P1/P2 priority ladder
nodes.rationale: P0 is the minimum set sufficient for the Winter Storm Uri Texas demo; P1 is the national scale slide; P2 is stretch. Nothing in P0 depends on gated sources (HIFLD/TAMU form).

nodes.label: Real vs slideware honesty ledger
nodes.rationale: C3 is real; C1 is real but proxy-laden; C2 is an estimate with a wide interval at best. Historical claims are only quotable if refuters pass, otherwise replaced by the C3 twin number which is what we actually control.

nodes.label: GET /layers/{name}
nodes.rationale: Static geometry cached as GeoJSON bytes at startup; scenario-dependent layers built per request and LRU-cached by (name, scenario_id, hour, run_id); Arrow IPC for time-series layers.

nodes.label: Arrow reshape (data/reshape.ts)
nodes.rationale: outage_risk Arrow reshaped once into Map<fips, Float32Array(hours)>; cascade JSON into trippedAtHour/darkAtHour maps for O(1) lookup during scrub.

nodes.label: EAGLE-I (ORNL outage dataset)
nodes.rationale: Ground truth for the outage model; high risk that Globus/ORNL access is slow — fallback is storm_events-derived pseudo-outages, stated honestly.

nodes.label: EAGLE-I county outages (S5)
nodes.rationale: Open on figshare CC BY 4.0; streamed through DuckDB read_csv with a Texas pushdown rather than pandas because files are 1.1-1.4 GB per year.

nodes.label: Cascade playback layer
nodes.rationale: Not a separate geometry layer: it drives lines (tripped set), outage_risk (dark counties) and a pulse on the bus tripping at exactly hour.

nodes.label: National H3 hex view
nodes.rationale: A scale slide, not an interactive product; 404 not_built hides the toggle; VITE_NATIONAL=1 keeps step 6 rehearsable.

nodes.label: OpenFreeMap basemap (PMTiles fallback)
nodes.rationale: Keyless public tiles; ship a Texas-extent PMTiles file in web/public as the fallback if OpenFreeMap is down at demo time.

nodes.label: MapboxOverlay interleaved mode
nodes.rationale: Interleaved so lines render under basemap labels via beforeId; read the symbol layer id at runtime, fall back to overlaid mode if none found.

nodes.label: hour is the single clock
nodes.rationale: Every time-dependent layer derives from (scenarioId, hour) via memoized selectors; scenario data is fetched once per scenario so the hour scrub never hits the network.

nodes.label: 60 fps scrub performance budget
nodes.rationale: Scrubbing must not re-upload geometry: only accessors change, keyed by updateTriggers on hour; per-frame work is O(n) hash lookups; escape hatch is a binary-attribute PathLayer. Never draw 82k buses as GeoJSON — that is what the hex layer is for.

nodes.label: EAGLE-I actual vs predicted split
nodes.rationale: Two DeckGL overlays are expensive; use one layer with a per-feature colour source switched by screen-x; fallback is a toggle plus county-card sparkline. Do not spend > 1 h on the split.

nodes.label: HeuristicOutageModel (fallback logistic)
nodes.rationale: Transparent hand-tuned logistic on the same features so the map is never empty; becomes authoritative if EAGLE-I is late or LightGBM Uri AUC < 0.70, and the slide says so.

nodes.label: twin.build.gen_unavailability
nodes.rationale: Cold-weather derates for uri_2021 (gas/coal 0.35, wind 0.5, nuclear 0.05) make the twin honest about Uri's real driver being generation loss, not only lines.

nodes.label: twin.build.line_failure_probs
nodes.rationale: p_fail = 1 - exp(-(lambda_wind + lambda_ice) * length_km) with kV-class fragility priors; priors are unverified against utility fragility curves — this is the physics layer, spec 02 is the calibrated layer.

nodes.label: Two heads: p_out classifier + tweedie frac regressor
nodes.norm_label: two heads: p_out classifier + tweedie frac regressor
nodes.rationale: Binary head gives probability, tweedie head on positives gives conditional fraction; frac_hat = p_out x E[frac|out]. Trained twice (nowcast vs forecast feature sets) because Storm Events and autoregressive terms are retrospective and unavailable at forecast time.

nodes.label: Uri was generation shortfall, not only wires
nodes.norm_label: uri was generation shortfall, not only wires
nodes.rationale: A weather->wires model under-predicts rolling blackouts; temp_min_48h/hours_below_m10 act as proxies while the cascade spec's generation-outage scenario is the physically honest layer.

nodes.label: C2 — Hardening/firm-generation effect estimate (DiD)
nodes.rationale: Two-way FE DiD with synthetic-control weights on restoration duration; with P0 data it is slideware with a number attached, only defensible with EIA-861 and 2018-2025 EAGLE-I. Never a point estimate without the CI; refuters reported not hidden.

nodes.label: MissingLoadHourError
nodes.rationale: A missing ba_load_hourly hour raises rather than silently falling back to the base case.

nodes.label: twin.cascade.run_cascade
nodes.rationale: Drop -> DC power flow -> trip all overloaded -> repeat up to MAX_STAGES; simultaneous trip is deterministic, trip_policy='worst' is the fallback if runs over-cascade.

nodes.label: twin.cascade.run_scenario
nodes.rationale: Runs run_cascade per hour carrying failures forward; net= override is the intervention hook used by siting and causal counterfactuals.

nodes.label: EIA-930 hourly BA demand (S4)
nodes.rationale: Only place EIA-930 touches physics: the twin scales every load by ERCO demand / SUM(p_mw_nominal).

nodes.label: Load scaling handoff to twin
nodes.rationale: loads.p_mw_nominal sums to the ~67 GW base case; the twin scales by ba_load_hourly.demand_mw(ERCO)/SUM(p_mw_nominal) so BA labeling errors affect labels, not physics.

nodes.label: Break-it mutation probes (trip_pct, zero failure probs)
nodes.norm_label: break-it mutation probes (trip_pct, zero failure probs)
nodes.rationale: Mutating trip_pct to 1e9 must drop overload trips to zero and zeroing line_failure_probs must drop weather trips to zero, proving the overload and weather wires are live, not decorative.

nodes.label: Explicit networkx islanding
nodes.rationale: pandapower's check_connectivity=True silently zeroes islands that have generation, so islands are found with nx.connected_components and one ext_grid is created per surviving island before rundcpp.

nodes.label: Two solver modes under a 120 s budget
nodes.norm_label: two solver modes under a 120 s budget
nodes.rationale: pandapower is 0.84 s/solve so hourly Uri (500-850 solves) is 7-12 min — too slow on stage. lightsim2grid is the default (expected >=20x); the pandapower fallback uses hour_stride=6 written into run_id so a strided run can never be mistaken for hourly. Exceeding budget raises CascadeBudgetExceeded with partial result, never silent truncation.
